title: Nontrivial single-server private information retrieval from one-way functions
formal: Does the existence of classical one-way functions imply a computationally private single-server private-information-retrieval protocol with sublinear communication and no client database preprocessing?
definitions: The client holds an index i into an n-bit database held by one server and must recover its bit, while the server cannot computationally distinguish requests for different indices. The client receives no database-dependent hint before the retrieval. Both parties use classical computation, and the intended security is against polynomial-time server distinguishers in the plain model. No public-key, homomorphic-encryption or ideal-oracle assumption is given in addition to one-way functions. The precise joint asymptotic communication/security convention remains to be fixed from the source; this is an admitted source draft, not a self-contained benchmark statement.

context_blocks.text: Nontrivial private retrieval separates communication from database size while hiding which item is requested. The assumption question asks how far this capability lies above one-way computation.

Single-server PIR implies oblivious transfer under appropriate nontriviality conditions. That implication does not supply a construction from arbitrary one-way functions. Results allowing a database-dependent client hint or preprocessing concern a different model.

why: A basic unresolved assumption relationship between one-way computation, public-key-style interaction and private access to data.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, preserving the quantifiers, model and guarantees. Conditional results settle only their conditional claims. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
